summary: A red-brick tower of about 175 feet, lit in 1887 on Ponce de Leon Inlet; the first tower, built in 1835, fell to erosion and the Seminole War, and Stephen Crane sighted this light from a dinghy.

notes_for_editor: Annual Reports of the Light-House Board for 1883-1887 are not in the local corpus, so the building chronology rests on the NHL nomination (which cites them) and the museum pages; check against the reports if possible. Disagreements stated in the story: Seminole raid 25 vs 26 Dec 1835; Williams salary $450; Rowlinski start date (13 Oct vs acting 21 Oct 1887); name change 1926 vs 1927; automation 1952 vs 1953; Babcock drowning 2 June vs Saturday 31 May 1884 (newspapers: one says 'yesterday at 2:30', one 'Saturday'); electricity 1923 'under Sisson' though he began 1924. Source 9 (1919 Bulletin) text is column-interleaved OCR; quotes are matched by position. LHB volume annualreportlig02statgoog holds 1896 and 1897 reports; the lightning item (795) could be either fiscal year, so the story says 'mid-1890s' and the date is not given. 'William Lindquist' (first assistant 1913-1916, and second assistant 1906-1908) is NOT claimed to be the keeper's son William T. Lindquist (born after 1897). Not used: museum claims Commodore sank about 13 miles offshore; Lighthouse Friends says the Open Boat crew rowed 27 hours while Crane says 30. Museum history says assistant positions were abolished in 1933, but the roster lists assistants to 1944. Georgetown and Amelia Island ids in other_stations: Amelia Island id us-fl-amelia-island exists in the data; Georgetown given without id. Matched by position on the Bulletin 1915 efficiency-flag table (column layout) for 'Mosquito Inlet, J. Lindquist'. Unnamed Coast Guard men not individually described. Photos not collected.
